conviction_note: Q3 fuel ran far above Delta's $3.15/gal guide assumption (Gulf Coast spot averaged about $3.84 in Q3, $4.39 in September). Consensus ($1.82-1.96) already sits below the $2.00-2.50 guide, and peers' September updates show fare recapture strong enough to offset much of the fuel gap. The print should land near the bar. The reaction turns on the Q4 guide against a single-source UBS whisper of $1.25-1.75. These findings net to a small negative, and p_up of 48 on a 5.5% absolute move scales to -0.22. The two measures agree in sign and the gap between them is small.
bar: Q3 adj. revenue about $17.6B (Bloomberg via Yahoo, https://www.aol.com/articles/delta-q3-earnings-preview-premium-153009000.html, 2026-10-08; TradingView $17.62B via https://www.optionstradingreport.com/2026/10/delta-faces-its-biggest-fuel-test-of-2026-options-price-an-8-move/). Q3 adj. EPS $1.82 (Bloomberg) / $1.88 (Yahoo, 19 analysts, https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/premium-tickets-could-help-delta-220700187.html) / $1.94-1.96 (https://parameter.io/delta-air-lines-dal-faces-rising-fuel-costs-as-q3-earnings-approach-october-9/). All are below the stale company guide of $2.00-2.50. The Q4 EPS bar has one source only: a UBS-reported Street expectation of $1.25-1.75 at $4.00-4.10/gal (parameter.io). Benzinga's $2.00-2.18 Q4 consensus looks stale. The Q4 finding is capped small for this reason.
positioning_check: Short interest about 29.1M shares, 3.01 days to cover at the 2026-06-30 settlement (curvedtrading, https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/dal/). Benzinga shows an undated 4.48% of float and 3.79 days. No September 2026 settlement was found. Not a crowded short. Skew is +0.71 vol points, balanced. Put/call OI is 0.12, so open interest is call-heavy. The stock is -2.86% over 5 days, +4.45% over 20 days, and 12.75% below its 52-week high. Q3 EPS consensus has been cut about 11% over 60 days.

findings.finding: Realised Q3 jet fuel ran far above the $3.15/gal all-in Delta set on the 2026-07-02 curve. EIA Gulf Coast spot averaged $3.40 in July, $3.72 in August and $4.39 in September (about $3.84 for the quarter). In Q2, $3.64 spot mapped to Delta's $3.93 all-in, so the Q3 overrun is roughly $0.6-0.9/gal on about 1.05B gallons, or $0.6-0.9B before recapture.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In July 2026 Delta beat Q2 while carrying a 75% fuel increase, affirmed FY, and the stock went -1.81%. In April 2026 (Q1 fuel shock, revenue raised in March) it went +3.75% (baseline).
findings.source_date: 2026-10-07 (EIA release of 2026-10-06 data; FRED MJFUELUSGULF confirms Jul 3.403 / Aug 3.724)
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. Consensus at $1.82-1.96 sits below the $2.00-2.50 guide, and UBS is at $1.70. Previews cite the $3.15 assumption without the realised September figure ($4.39 average, peaking at $4.71 on Sep 15). Delta has filed no 8-K since 2026-07-10 (EDGAR submissions), so it has not quantified the gap. If the full September spike were priced, consensus would sit nearer UBS's $1.70.
findings.independence: JetBlue's 8-K of 2026-09-10 raised its Q3 fuel assumption from $3.49 to $3.96 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001158463/000115846326000089/jblu-20260910.htm). United's 2026-07-15 update put Q3 at $3.69 after a $575M jump from early July (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000100517/000010051726000135/ual_erx06302026xex992.htm). These are industry proxies, not Delta's own number.

findings.finding: Peers that spoke after Delta's July guide reported fare recapture above plan. On 2026-09-10 JetBlue raised Q3 RASM to +17-20% from +12.5-16.5%, a 4-point midpoint lift, with 'no meaningful signs of elasticity'. On Sep 16 American's CEO felt 'really good' about +16-19% Q3 revenue. That points to Delta revenue above the +15.7% consensus, offsetting much of the fuel overrun.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 revenue of $17.67B slightly missed $17.76B (parameter.io) while EPS beat, and the stock went -1.81%. Delta's revenue beats have not been rewarded much on their own.
findings.why_not_priced: Revenue consensus of $17.6B (+15.7%) still sits inside Delta's own July 'mid-teens' guide, so the Street has not moved revenue up for the peer RASM upgrades. If it had, the revenue bar would be about $17.9-18.0B (+17-18%).
findings.independence: American CEO Isom at Morgan Stanley Laguna, Sep 16 (Reuters syndication, https://wsau.com/?p=1017112). BLS: airline fares +25.5% y/y in July (https://www.bls.gov/opub/ted/2026/summer-vacations-prices-for-gasoline-and-air-travel-each-up-more-than-20-percent-over-the-year.htm). Peer proxies, not Delta's own number.

findings.finding: JetBlue's 2026-09-10 8-K raised Q3 CASM-ex to +6-8% from +2.5-4.5%, citing Northeast weather and ATC disruption in July and August. Delta's JFK, LGA and BOS operations were exposed to the same constraints, which threatens the 'modest improvement' in non-fuel unit cost Delta guided for Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean prior CASM-only surprise is visible in the baseline.
findings.why_not_priced: Previews focus on fuel and premium demand. None of the Delta previews read mentions Northeast operational cost. Delta's footprint outside the Northeast dilutes the effect, so the finding is sized small.
findings.independence: Same JetBlue document as the RASM finding, read for a different line (cost, not revenue). No second source.

findings.finding: On 2026-10-06 Gulf Coast jet spot was $4.34/gal, down from the $4.71 peak on Sep 15 but still about 8% above early September. On the Q2 spot-to-all-in mapping, Delta's Q4 all-in lands near or above the top of the $4.00-4.10 range behind the Street's Q4 EPS expectation of $1.25-1.75. That leans the Q4 guide toward the lower half of the whisper.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: January 2026: Q4 beat, but the 2026 guide fell short of hopes, and the stock went -2.39%. July 2026: FY affirmed despite fuel, -1.81%. The guide drives this name's reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The UBS whisper already assumes $4.00-4.10. The edge is only whether Delta's forward-curve all-in lands above that, and the refinery gain (UBS: 40-45c/gal, against only 11c realised in Q2) could pull it either way. If priced, Q4 consensus would already read about $1.50 rather than the $2.00+ some aggregators still show.
findings.independence: American CFO May (Sep 16): Q4 fuel about $1/gal above July's assumption, about $1B (https://wsau.com/?p=1017112). The bar comes from a single source (UBS via https://parameter.io/delta-air-lines-dal-faces-rising-fuel-costs-as-q3-earnings-approach-october-9/), so this finding is capped small.

findings.finding: Bastian said Delta does not 'want to be with Elon Musk'. Musk said Delta 'will lose a lot of customers', and United and American, which carry Starlink, are running status-match challenges aimed at Delta's Medallion members. This is a premium-share question likely to be raised on the call.
findings.why_not_priced: It is in the Yahoo preview, so it is largely priced as a story. Any quantified effect on premium share would not show up until Q4 bookings commentary.

findings.finding: CEO Bastian sold about $19.2M of stock in early August 2026 (Form 4s and 144s filed 2026-08-03 to 08-06). He made a similar sale after the July 2025 print, so this is a routine post-earnings-window sale.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: A $19.7M sale in July 2025 was followed by a +4.29% reaction in October 2025 (baseline, https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/delta-air-lines-inc-nysedal-ceo-sells-196980000-in-stock-2025-07-24).
findings.why_not_priced: Public for two months and a pattern seen before, so essentially priced. Filed because it is a sourced fact; sized near zero.
findings.independence: EDGAR submissions list Form 4s on 2026-08-05/06 and 144s on 2026-08-03..05 (https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0000027904.json).

baseline_tension: The findings net slightly negative against a balanced skew (+0.71), call-heavy open interest and a 5-day pullback. Consensus has already been cut 11%, which absorbs most of the fuel news, so p_up is held near 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6 (bar): the Q4 EPS bar has one source (a UBS-reported whisper), so the Q4 guide finding was capped from -0.6 to -0.4.
Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a predicted reaction): Delta's revenue and EPS beats have been sold (Q2 -1.81%, Jan -2.39%), so the peer-recapture revenue finding was cut from +0.9 to +0.6.
Lesson 5 (proxy): the Q3 fuel finding rests on Gulf Coast spot, not Delta's own number, and the consensus below the guide already reflects it, so it was cut from -0.7 to -0.5.
Lesson 7: short interest about 3 days to cover is not crowded and skew is balanced, so no change to the negative findings or p_up. CASM, Starlink and insider findings unchanged.
